steps.tx: **Classic lichen planus** manifests as the memorable six Ps: pruritic, planar, polygonal, purple, papules, and plaques. Lesions consist of flat-topped violaceous shiny papules with a subtle network of white lacy lines on their surface known as Wickham striae, best visualised after applying a drop of mineral oil.
steps.say: The classic morphology features flat-topped, polygonal, violaceous papules that cause intense pruritus. Delicate white streaks called Wickham striae are visible across the surface under magnification.

vis.alt: Lichen planus violaceous papules and interface dermatitis histology.
vis.caption: Lichen planus polygonal papules showing Wickham striae and dense interface dermatitis.

steps.tx: **Koebner phenomenon** commonly occurs in active lichen planus, where linear configurations of new violaceous papules appear along lines of mechanical scratching or superficial trauma. Predilection sites include the flexor aspects of the wrists, forearms, lumbar back, anterior lower legs, and the glans penis in males.
steps.say: Scratching or friction prompts new isomorphic papules in a linear pattern, confirming the Koebner phenomenon. Lesions favour the volar wrists, ankles, lumbar spine, and genitalia.

steps.tx: **Oral lichen planus** affects the buccal mucosa in over half of all patients, presenting as reticular asymptomatic white lace-like patterns. Less commonly, erosive oral disease produces painful ulcerations and desquamative gingivitis, carrying a small documented long-term risk of malignant transformation into oral squamous cell carcinoma.
steps.say: Reticular oral involvement creates asymptomatic white streaks over the buccal mucosa. Chronic erosive mucosal disease is painful and requires surveillance due to long-term squamous carcinoma risk.

steps.tx: **Civatte bodies** represent apoptotic, necrotic basal keratinocytes shed into the lower epidermis and papillary dermis on histopathology. Tissue biopsy reveals dense, band-like lymphocytic infiltration hugging the dermoepidermal junction, liquefactive degeneration of the basal layer, irregular saw-toothed epidermal hyperplasia, and prominent wedge-shaped hypergranulosis.
steps.say: Histology demonstrates a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate obscuring the dermoepidermal junction. Basal cell necrosis generates eosinophilic Civatte colloid bodies alongside saw-toothed rete ridges.

nodes.label: Apoptotic keratinocytes condense into Civatte bodies
Band-like infiltrate produces saw-toothed epidermal remodeling

steps.tx: **Dorsal pterygium** forms when the proximal nail fold adheres pathologically to the nail bed, resulting in longitudinal splitting and permanent loss of the nail plate. Twenty-nail dystrophy and thinning with longitudinal ridging can also develop, while scalp lichen planopilaris causes progressive cicatricial alopecia.
steps.say: Severe nail involvement produces dorsal pterygium, where the proximal fold fuses to the nail bed with plate destruction. Follicular lichen planopilaris causes irreversible scarring hair loss.

vis.caption: Lichen planopilaris with follicular plugging, peripilar casts, and perifollicular fibrosis.

steps.tx: **Pityriasis rosea** represents an acute, benign, self-limited papulosquamous eruption primarily affecting young adults, likely triggered by human herpesvirus 6 or 7 reactivation. An initial solitary salmon-pink oval plaque called the herald patch precedes widespread smaller oval lesions aligned along skin cleavage lines.
steps.say: Pityriasis rosea begins with a single larger herald patch on the trunk. Days later, secondary eruptive plaques align along relaxed skin cleavage lines without systemic compromise.

vis.title: Pityriasis Rosea Diagnostic Profile
rows: Fir tree pattern along Langer lines
Follows rib cage obliquely on back

steps.tx: **Christmas tree pattern** describes the classic distribution of secondary pityriasis rosea plaques across the thoracic trunk and back. Each oval lesion features a delicate, inward-facing collarette of scale along its margin. The condition resolves spontaneously within six to eight weeks without scarring.
steps.say: The trunk eruption follows Langer cleavage lines obliquely, resembling the branches of a Christmas tree. Individual plaques exhibit an inward-facing collarette of fine trailing scale.

nodes.label: Herald patch appears on trunk or proximal thigh
Subclinical viral reactivation interval of 7 to 14 days
Eruptive oval plaques disperse in Christmas tree layout
Spontaneous complete desquamation by week eight

steps.tx: **Islands of normal skin** constitute the striking diagnostic clue in pityriasis rubra pilaris, an uncommon chronic papulosquamous disorder. Red-orange follicular hyperkeratotic papules coalesce into extensive erythroderma that spares distinct round patches of uninvolved pale skin, accompanied by thickened waxy orange palmoplantar keratoderma.
steps.say: Pityriasis rubra pilaris features widespread reddish-orange plaques containing discrete islands of unaffected normal skin. Severe waxy hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles is typical.
